title: Sarawak Energy Marathon 2026 Review: A Flat 1am Marathon Run in Haze
seo_title: Sarawak Energy Marathon Review: Course, Haze, Cut-offs
meta_description: Sarawak Energy Marathon 2026 review: the flat Kuching course, a 1am start, 94% humidity and an unhealthy API of 153 at 8am, the cut-offs, aid, roads and how fast the field ran.
dek: What running Kuching's August marathon was like in 2026: the flat night course, the humidity and the haze, the cut-offs and aid, the part-closed roads, and how fast you need to be to place.
verdict: Enter if you want a cheap, AIMS-certified night marathon in Borneo and can cope with wet, still air. The 2026 race drew a record 8,535 runners to Kuching, sent the marathon off at 1am on a course that barely rises above 20 m, and gave it seven hours. Early-bird entry was RM90, and registration fees went to charity. The catch in 2026 was the air: haze was reported from 4am, humidity sat at 94% with a 23°C dew point, and the air-pollutant index was 153, in the unhealthy range, at 8am. Entries are non-refundable even if haze forces a cancellation, so watch the readings in the days before you travel.

sections.heading: The Course: A Flat Night Route Through Old Kuching
paragraphs: Both certified races start and finish at Menara Sarawak Energy on the Kuching Isthmus [1]. The organiser's route takes runners past the Darul Hana Bridge, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Building, the Borneo Cultures Museum, the Kuching cat statue and the Kuching Waterfront [2]. The police closure list for race night names about 30 roads, among them Jalan Pending, Jalan Padungan, Jalan Main Bazaar, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, Jalan Satok, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Astana [3].

It is flat. On the official 42 km elevation profile the course stays mostly between about 5 m and 15 m above sea level, and its highest points, just over 20 m, come near 20 km and 25 km [3]. The 21 km and 42 km courses are AIMS-certified [4]. The full marathon is still new: it was added in 2025 [5].
With a 1am flag-off and a seven-hour limit, most of the marathon is run in the dark.

sections.heading: The Weather and the Haze: 94% Humidity and an Unhealthy API
paragraphs: Kuching International Airport, about 9 km south of the start, recorded 27°C, a dew point of 25°C, 89% humidity and a 2-knot wind at 1am, when the marathon started [6]. By the 4am half-marathon start it was 25°C with a 23°C dew point, and the airport began reporting haze. From 5.30am to 8am it held at 24°C and 94% humidity with almost no wind, and haze was reported in every observation from 4am to 9.30am [6].
Those temperatures are mild for a tropical marathon, but a dew point of 23°C to 25°C means sweat barely evaporates, so the flat profile flatters less than it looks. Pace by effort from the start.

The haze was the bigger issue. The organiser said it was monitoring conditions and went ahead; at 8am, the time all three competitive races closed, Kuching's air-pollutant index (API) was 153, inside the unhealthy band of 101 to 200 [7]. Malaysia's health advice once the API passes 100 is for the general public to reduce strenuous outdoor activity, and school sports events are postponed [7]. A Borneo Post public-health column later asked whether organisers have clear enough thresholds for such decisions, while saying the question was not whether a rule had been broken [7].

The haze went on after the race. A half marathon in Sarikei set for 23 August was cancelled on health advice [7], and on 25 September the Kuching Marathon, with more than 13,000 entrants, was called off two days before race day [8].

sections.heading: Start Times, Cut-offs and Aid
paragraphs: The marathon started at 1am, the half marathon at 4am, the 10 km at 5.45am and the 5 km fun run at 6.15am [1]. The limits are seven hours for the marathon, four hours for the half, 2 hours 15 minutes for the 10 km and 1 hour 30 minutes for the 5 km [9], so the three competitive races all close at 8am. There are checkpoint cut-offs along the way, strictly enforced; runners who miss one are disqualified and may be taken back on the organiser's transport. Runners who do not start within 15 minutes of their flag-off may not be allowed to race [9].
The official marathon map shows about 14 aid points, each marked for water, isotonic drink, a medic and toilets, with energy gel at one of them [3].

Every entrant gets an event T-shirt, and finishers get a medal; marathon and half-marathon runners inside the limit also get a finisher T-shirt [10], which has to be collected at the finish [9]. The first 100 finishers in each of the marathon and half, by gun time and regardless of gender, get a special-edition top-finisher T-shirt, and e-certificates can be downloaded within two weeks [9].

sections.heading: The Roads: Partly Closed Until 10am
paragraphs: Most of the route is on partly closed roads. Police closed or diverted about 30 roads, most of them from just after midnight to 8am on race day [3]. Only the stretch between the Kuching Isthmus Bridge and the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching was fully closed, from 8am on the Saturday to 10am on the Sunday. Elsewhere the partial closures were lifted as runners cleared each section, with all roads due to reopen by 10am, and traffic police and Rela members were posted at the affected points [1].
The rules say the marathon's partial closures are lifted seven hours after the start [9]. If you expect to be near the limit, expect traffic to return around you in the last hour.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Vietnam's Pham Thi Hong Le won the women's marathon in 2:47:48 [11]. The men's race was led home by four Kenyans and a Vietnamese runner; Malaysia's Ni Jia was sixth and won the national title [12]. No men's winning time had been published by late September. In 2025, the first year of the marathon, Kenyans filled the men's podium in 2:22:10 to 2:23:30, and Caroline Cherono won the women's race in 2:43:16 [13].

Prize money brings the fast runners: RM201,500 in total [4], with RM15,000 for each open marathon winner [2], paid to the top 15 in each category of the marathon, half and 10 km [9]. Malaysians in the marathon are also ranked in a separate national category and can win from both, and runners aged 45 and over can race as veterans [9].
For everyone else the realistic target is the top-100 T-shirt [9]. By early June nearly 500 people had entered the marathon [2]; the final marathon field was not published.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: For the night start, free shuttles ran from the Riverside Majestic bus stop to the BCCK roundabout from 11.30pm on the Saturday to 5am, with return buses from 8am to 10am every 20 minutes [1].

Early-bird fees in 2026 were RM90 for the marathon, RM70 for the half, RM60 for the 10 km and RM40 for the 5 km [14], and 2026 entries closed on 30 June [2]. All registration proceeds go to Sarawak charities; the 2026 race raised RM480,000 for 16 of them, RM30,000 each [4]. There was a race village with food stalls and family activities, and a lucky draw [4][2].

Fees are non-refundable, and entries cannot be transferred or switched to another distance. If the race is cancelled or postponed for force majeure or public-health reasons, no refunds are given [9]. Marathon runners must be 18 or over and half-marathon runners 16 or over [9].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a flat, certified marathon for a low fee and can sleep before a 1am start. The half marathon, with four hours and a finisher T-shirt, suits a first-timer, and fast runners have prize money 15 deep to aim for.

Think twice if you have asthma or a heart or breathing condition. August 2026 brought haze to Kuching, the race ran with an unhealthy API reading, and the rules give no refund if the race is cancelled for public-health reasons [9]. Watch the API in the week before, and have a plan for pulling out.
The 2027 race is on Sunday 8 August [4]. Fees, start times and any haze policy for 2027 had not been published by late September 2026.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's releases, race rules and route map, airport weather records, local news reports in English, a Vietnamese news report, and a running outlet's post on the results.

pull_quotes.quote: Knowing that the air is unhealthy is only the first step.
pull_quotes.attribution: Dr Melvin Ebin Bondi, public health columnist, The Borneo Post, writing on the August 2026 haze

faqs.question: What time does the Sarawak Energy Marathon start?
faqs.answer: At 1am for the full marathon. In 2026 the half marathon started at 4am, the 10 km at 5.45am and the 5 km fun run at 6.15am, all from Menara Sarawak Energy on the Kuching Isthmus. Free shuttles ran from the Riverside Majestic bus stop between 11.30pm and 5am.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Sarawak Energy Marathon?
faqs.answer: Seven hours for the marathon, four hours for the half marathon, 2 hours 15 minutes for the 10 km and 1 hour 30 minutes for the 5 km in 2026, so the three competitive races all closed at 8am. Checkpoint cut-offs on the course are strictly enforced, and runners who miss one are disqualified.

faqs.question: Was the 2026 Sarawak Energy Marathon affected by haze?
faqs.answer: Yes. The race went ahead while the organiser monitored the haze. Kuching airport reported haze from 4am, and Kuching's air-pollutant index was 153, in the unhealthy range, at 8am. Entry fees are not refunded even if the race is cancelled for public-health reasons, so check the readings before you travel.

faqs.question: Is the Sarawak Energy Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. On the official elevation profile the marathon stays mostly between about 5 m and 15 m above sea level, with its highest points just over 20 m near 20 km and 25 km. The 21 km and 42 km courses are AIMS-certified, and both start and finish at Menara Sarawak Energy.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to win at the Sarawak Energy Marathon?
faqs.answer: Very fast. In 2026 the women's marathon was won in 2:47:48, and four Kenyans and a Vietnamese runner took the top five men's places. In 2025 the men's winner ran 2:22:10. Open marathon winners get RM15,000, and prize money goes to the top 15 in each category.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the 2026 edition, run on 9 August; replaces the 2026-09-28 version. Weather is from Kuching airport METAR observations, about 9 km from the start, not a forecast. The API reading is from a Borneo Post column (read via its Wayback Machine copy; the site returned 403). The official race site refused connections, so its rules and FAQ are cited from archived April and May 2026 copies. Full results were behind a bot check and no men's winning time was found, so only the women's winner and the men's finishing order from a running outlet are given. The organiser gave 8,535 registrations after the race and 8,544 the day before; the later figure is used. The 5 km start was 6.30am in the April rules and 6.15am in the race-week statement; the latter is used. Aid points were counted on a low-resolution map image and are given as approximate. No rating.
